source.snippet: I manage a WordPress-based gaming news website hosted on shared Linux hosting. Since September 2026, I've noticed a significant increase in the average response time reported by Google Search Console, along with a reduction in Googlebot's crawling activity. Late July: ~569ms. August: ~740ms. September: ~1,128ms. October: higher. [0 score, 1 comment]

problem_statement: Small website operators on shared hosting see SEO-damaging server response time degradation after platform updates or increased load but lack actionable diagnostic tooling that correlates hosting performance metrics with Googlebot crawl rate changes and revenue impact.
target_segment: Small-to-mid blog and media site operators (1–5 person teams) on shared or budget managed WordPress hosting monetizing via ads or affiliate
notes: Site owner is clearly losing crawl budget and likely ad revenue; they are already paying for hosting and likely paying for SEO tools (Ahrefs, SEMrush). A lightweight diagnostic-and-fix SaaS specifically bridging GSC data + hosting performance for non-technical WordPress operators could command $20-50/mo. Multiple similar questions appear repeatedly across webmaster forums.
